study.question: Can auxiliary tasks contribute through a small deterministic event-relevance gate without reopening their harmful gradient paths into primary item representations? Does the donor need protection from click gradients?
study.hypothesis: Observation: round9 event gating achieved click AUC0.6624770287 versus uniform-gain0.6618218327; collapsed-identity event gating achieved0.6624545972. Thus event binding has local single-seed support, while extra feedback identity has only a0.0000224315 contrast. Earlier primary-owned item tables outperformed joint ones; round7 sharing label-related fields fell to0.6592436764 versus private0.6601638278. Round6 dense auxiliary transfer reached0.6592574965 versus self0.6588211471, both below private parent0.6601638278. Those failed transfers do not refute all possible interaction stages. The existing gates are independent per-task functions of a shared interpretable20-dimensional event feature space. Transferring only auxiliary gate preactivations may convey useful event utility without aligning dense private representations. Detaching that donor may preserve its auxiliary supervision. This is an uncertain training-information-flow hypothesis in an unchanged function class, not a prediction that more capacity or additional feedback labels at inference improve quality.

nearest_work.difference: Primary text section4.3 lines250-277 inspected: target-conditioned unnormalized local-activation pooling is inherited from the adapted baseline. Proposed cross-task gate preactivation transfer/gradient ownership is an added local intervention; no exact original DIN reproduction or priority claim.

Pinned benchmark source lines123-169 and188-273 inspected. Its masked feedback sequence hubs, task/shared tokens and repeated aggregation/broadcast provide the nearest inspected task-aware flow reference. Here only a deterministic20-feature gate sends one scalar per event to click, with private embedding paths unchanged; no token/hub stack is reproduced.

Original paper is available as link/provenance only in the authorized registry; original full-text mechanism and priority remain unverified. Benchmark fallback was inspected explicitly as a separate source.

Local receipt shows detached dense auxiliary-tower residual transfer failed against its private parent. This proposal instead mixes existing pre-tanh event gate scalars, adds zero parameters, and crosses donor identity with donor gradient ownership. The r6 result is contextual evidence, not a matched control for this stage.

inherited_components: Round9 resolved event gate: four task rows by20 deterministic exposure/feedback x category/brand match features; bounded1+tanh gain and strict history masking.
Round8 forty count/fraction features and per-task additive logit correction; original target action is never consumed.
Round5 learned private auxiliary item/action tables and shared user/context; primary item tables and primary-owned128/32 Dice selector trunk with separate task score rows.
Task prediction towers128/64, embedding_dim16, current target fields and all host protocol/data/optimization contracts.
study.proposed_difference: For each valid event let z_t=W_t*phi with the existing4x20 zero-initialized gate matrix. Set donor_aux=(z_cart+z_fav+z_buy)/3 or donor_self=z_click. Only click uses gain1+tanh(z_click+0.5*D(donor)); other tasks retain1+tanh(z_t). D is stop-gradient or identity, making a2x2 factorial. No extra weights, random initialization, donor projection, current labels, teacher checkpoints or loss reweighting. Task order is resolved through the existing label buffer. Masked events have gain1 and score0; empty-history pooling and corrections remain0. All variants start exactly at the parent function. At fixed weights donor detachment leaves forward values unchanged. For detached auxiliary transfer the explicit click-to-donor gate edge is blocked; for live it is enabled. Shared context and dense clipping remain indirect coupling paths. Since mixing only linear gate logits changes the supervision geometry within the same function class, representation-capacity improvement and novel architecture claims are expressly unsupported.
predictions: Primary discriminant: gate_aux_detached should exceed both gate_self_detached and the no-transfer incumbent on full-population click AUC if auxiliary event utility provides useful complementary training signal. Assess click Logloss jointly and report all four task metrics; no numerical improvement is assumed.

Ownership prediction: stopping the explicit click gradient into auxiliary donor rows should better preserve auxiliary event relevance than live transfer. Compare this with the self live/detached contrast to expose simple gate-gradient scaling.

Expected scope: any direct gain from this mechanism appears for nonempty histories, potentially more clearly in the predeclared17-64 and>64 bins. Empty-history rows have exactly no direct donor effect, though shared trained parameters can change predictions. Treat slices as exploratory and report sample/positive/negative counts.

Expected allocated capacity remains56,349,784 parameters in every cell. Training cost should be close to round9 approximately498 seconds per complete train/validation unit; this is an estimate, not a measurement. No speedup is claimed.
falsifiers: If auxiliary transfer does not outperform the matched self replacement, complementary donor information is unsupported even if either beats the incumbent.
If live/detached changes are reproduced by the self-only gradient-scale contrast, evidence for auxiliary specialization protection is insufficient.

A zero-initialized variant that differs from the incumbent before any update, changed auxiliary forward logits at fixed inherited weights, label-order dependence, padded-input sensitivity or forbidden-input dependence fails integrity/preflight and must be repaired before interpretation; failed costs remain charged.

If paired repetition reverses the ranking, treat this single-seed proposal outcome as unstable. If donor transfer costs or memory prevent complete frozen-protocol execution within budget, report infeasibility separately from scientific counterevidence.
alternative_explanations: The gate gains in round9 may primarily reflect target matching and not distinct feedback types; near-equivalence under identity collapse argues against assuming strong auxiliary-specific complementarity.

Forward gate scaling, AdamW preconditioning, gradient covariance, saturation and global dense clipping may explain improvements. The four variants preserve capacity and include self and gradient controls, but these controls do not eliminate every optimizer confound.

Auxiliary tasks are category/brand-window labels rather than direct advertisement conversion attribution; correlated broad-interest evidence may transfer only under the released offline visibility policy.

Single-seed sampling, validation selection after many trials and changes propagated through shared context can mimic a transfer benefit. No bootstrap predictions, gradient telemetry, dynamic masking checks or withheld data are available in this proposal jail.

Current sources establish DIN and pinned benchmark provenance, not exhaustive nearest-work coverage; original INFNet and generic multi-task gating priority remain unverified. No novelty claim is made.
